from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Eigenbasis acts as a custom coordinate system.",
            "Standard basis vectors change directions unpredictably.",
            "Eigenbasis makes matrix math simple diagonal.",
            "Transformations look like simple scaling now.",
            "Rotating the camera reveals this structure."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Eigenbasis", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create visual elements
        eigenvecs = VGroup(
            Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT + UP, color="#FF6347"),
            Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 2 - UP, color="#FF6347")
        )
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        self.place_in_area(eigenvecs, "B2", "D4")
        self.play(Create(eigenvecs))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))
        self.place_in_area(grid, "B2", "D4")
        self.play(Create(grid), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        highlight = grid.copy().set_color("#FFFF00").set_stroke(width=4)
        self.add(highlight)
        self.play(Flash(highlight))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#BA55D3"))
        self.play(grid.animate.stretch(1.5, dim=0).stretch(0.8, dim=1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.play(Rotate(grid, angle=PI/6))
        self.play(FadeOut(grid), FadeOut(eigenvecs), FadeOut(highlight))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The 'Search Engine' Perspective", 
                          ["Eigenvectors simplify massive data sets effectively.", 
                           "Principal eigenvalues highlight major data trends.", 
                           "PageRank ranks influence using principal eigenvectors."])
        
        # Nodes for web graph
        nodes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.15, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(6)])
        node_positions = ["A2", "A5", "C1", "C6", "E2", "E5"]
        for node, pos in zip(nodes, node_positions):
            self.place_at_grid(node, pos)
        
        # Connections
        edges = VGroup(
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[1].get_center(), stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[1].get_center(), nodes[3].get_center(), stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[4].get_center(), stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[3].get_center(), nodes[5].get_center(), stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[4].get_center(), nodes[5].get_center(), stroke_width=2),
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(nodes), Create(edges))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        flow = VGroup(*[Dot(node.get_center(), color="#00FF00") for node in nodes])
        self.play(FadeIn(flow))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        highlight = nodes[5].copy().set_color("#FF00FF").set_stroke(width=4)
        label = Text("PageRank", font_size=20, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(label, "F6")
        self.play(Create(highlight), Write(label))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Matrices are functions changing vector spaces.", 
            "Eigenvectors are invariant axes of transformation.", 
            "Eigenvalues measure transformation intensity along axes."
        ])
        
        # Visualization objects
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_numbers": False})
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        vec1 = Vector([1, 1], color=RED)
        vec2 = Vector([-1, 1], color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(vec1, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(vec2, 'C4')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.play(grid.animate.apply_matrix([[1.5, 0.5], [0.5, 1.5]]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        # Show eigenvectors
        self.play(FadeIn(vec1), FadeIn(vec2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Emphasize intensity
        self.play(vec1.animate.scale(1.5), vec2.animate.scale(0.5))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Eigenvectors, Eigenvalues, and Eigenbasis: The Geometry of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Stretch' Concept
sections.content: Introduce linear transformation as a visual deformation of a 2D grid. Most vectors change direction when a matrix acts on them. We identify the 'special' vectors that remain on their original span—only scaled.
sections.example: Imagine a logo on a rubber sheet; when you stretch the sheet, most points shift diagonally, but points along the axis of the stretch stay on that line.

sections.title: Defining Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
sections.content: Formalize the equation Av = λv. Define 'Eigenvector' (v) as the direction that doesn't change, and 'Eigenvalue' (λ) as the factor by which it is stretched or squashed. Use a visual animation where v stays locked on a line.
sections.example: If matrix A represents a transformation, and v is an eigenvector with λ=2, the vector v simply doubles in length.

sections.title: Visualizing Eigenbasis
sections.content: Explain that an Eigenbasis is a set of eigenvectors that act as a 'special coordinate system.' In this basis, the complex transformation matrix A becomes a simple diagonal matrix, making calculations much faster.
sections.example: Switching from standard (x, y) coordinates to (v1, v2) coordinates is like rotating your camera to align with the stretch of the rubber sheet, making the transformation look like simple scaling.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The 'Search Engine' Perspective
sections.content: Briefly connect the abstract math to practical utility. Explain how identifying the most significant eigenvalues helps in simplifying data (dimensionality reduction/PCA).
sections.example: Think of a social network: the 'principal eigenvector' of a connection matrix identifies the most influential people (PageRank) based on how their influence scales across the network.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: A matrix is just a function. Eigenvectors are the 'invariant axes' of that function, and eigenvalues tell us the 'intensity' of the transformation along those axes.
sections.example: A quick visual animation: A square grid transforming into a rectangle, highlighting the two eigenvectors remaining fixed as the grid scales.
